Robert Short just won the job running Wyoming’s elections, promising voters he’d make the secretary of state’s office “boring again.” Weeks later, his first personnel decision is anything but boring — or Republican.

Short tapped Cara Boyle Chambers, a two-decade state government veteran, to serve as his 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐭𝐲 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞, the No. 2 post overseeing how the state runs its elections. Federal Election Commission records show Chambers has sent money to ActBlue, to Joe Biden’s 2020 campaign, and to multiple 2026 Democrat Senate candidates — including Maine’s Graham Platner, the Nazi-tattooed oyster farmer whose campaign collapsed under sexual misconduct allegations.

Confronted with her own donation trail, Chambers didn’t deny a word of it. She just offered Short an out: “𝘐𝘧 𝘐 𝘥𝘰 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘳𝘺 𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘵𝘶𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘭 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘶𝘵𝘰𝘳𝘺 𝘥𝘶𝘵𝘪𝘦𝘴 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘰𝘧𝘧𝘪𝘤𝘦, 𝘚𝘖𝘚-𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘤𝘵 𝘚𝘩𝘰𝘳𝘵 𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘮𝘺 𝘦𝘮𝘱𝘭𝘰𝘺𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵,” she told Cowboy State Daily — as if bankrolling Biden and ActBlue while running Wyoming’s elections is a problem to fix later, not a decision Short had already made.

Short’s own defense wasn’t any sturdier. He claimed “𝘯𝘰 𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘢” about her donor history, then waved it off anyway as “100% 𝘪𝘳𝘳𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘵 𝘵𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘫𝘰𝘣.” Chambers’ own party registration reportedly read Republican only as recently as September — despite her voting in Wyoming’s Democrat primaries in both 2022 and 2024.

This isn’t a one-off. Short’s own primary campaign ran on an in-kind donation from a Democrat state representative, and the very same week he hired Chambers, incoming GOP Gov. Eric Barlow named a 𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐜𝐫𝐚𝐭 to be the state’s next attorney general. In deep-red Wyoming, where the Republican primary is effectively the general election, that’s not an accident — it’s the 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐲𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐥𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐫𝐮𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 to control your state from inside the label on your own ballot.

𝐘𝐨𝐮 𝐯𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐞𝐨𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐫𝐮𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐞𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐥𝐚𝐰𝐬 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧’𝐭 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐣𝐨𝐛.

text:
The People Who Weave Themselves Into the Fabric of Our Lives ❤️

Today, after days of rain, the skies finally cleared enough for me to take Toby for a walk around our neighborhood. As I walked past the puddles reflecting the world around me, my thoughts wandered to familiar faces I no longer see. People I didn’t necessarily know personally, yet somehow, over the years, they quietly became part of the fabric of my life.

I thought about Don Ramon, affectionately known as “The Cross Guy,” who faithfully walked our boulevard carrying a large cross on his back. I would honk and wave whenever I passed him, and sometimes stop to offer him water. I understand his health has declined, and I pray he is doing well. Then there was the elderly Asian couple who walked together every morning around 10:30 to feed the ducks at the pond. For years, they were a familiar sight, until one day, there was only her. I often wondered what happened to him.

And I remembered the elderly gentleman who was always outside cutting lawns, greeting me with a smile and a wave as I walked Molly, long before Toby came into my life. Today, I passed the home where he and his wife once lived. The yard was overgrown, the house dark and quiet, and I wondered where life had taken them.

Isn’t it remarkable how people we barely know can leave such lasting impressions on our hearts? We don’t always realize how much their simple presence means until they’re no longer there. As we grow older, perhaps we begin to measure time differently — not just by birthdays and calendars, but by the familiar faces we no longer see, the routines that disappear, and the houses that grow quiet.

Maybe today, I wasn’t simply walking through my neighborhood. I was walking through years of memories. The puddles reflected the world above them, while my heart reflected on the world as it used to be. And it occurred to me that these people may never know they were remembered today, on an ordinary November afternoon, by someone walking her dog.

We may be just a passing face in someone’s day, yet become a lasting memory in their lifetime. ❤️

text:
What happened in markets today:

1. A rough Friday to end a rough week. $SPY fell 3.70% to 6,910.39, down 265 points, a seventh straight loss and now in correction territory, more than 10% off the record close. The selling was not subtle and it did not let up into the close.

2. Tech took the worst of it. $QQQ tracked a Nasdaq Composite that plunged 5.28%, losing 1,261 points to 22,617.73, the second biggest one day points drop in its history. That wipes out the gain for the year, with the index now down close to 3% in 2026. $DIA held up better on less tech weight but still fell 1.93%, down 950 points to 48,147.33, also in correction territory.

3. $NVDA was the center of the storm, down 14% on the day and 23% for the week, the worst day in almost two years. Reports of a widening SEC accounting probe landed on a stock already under pressure, and the selling spread fast through the whole AI trade. Strong numbers earlier in the week did not calm anyone down, and that says a lot about the mood right now.

4. The chip and memory rout was broad. $SNDK fell 16%, $AMD dropped 13%, and Micron and Western Digital both posted double digit losses. The semiconductor funds fell around 11% to 13%. When the leaders get hit this hard, the rest of the group rarely gets a pass, and Friday was no exception.

5. @AnthropicAI had a second day to forget. $ANT fell 8.5% to $88.91, coming within cents of the $83 IPO price at the low after a huge debut on Thursday. A record IPO was meant to steady the AI trade, and instead the fade added to the nerves. Worth watching whether that IPO price holds next week, since a break below it would keep the pressure on sentiment.

6. Earnings offered no shelter either. $BJ beat on the headline, with adjusted EPS of $1.73 against $1.26 expected and revenue up 18% to $6.28B against $5.97B expected, and the full year guide went up to $5.10 to $5.30. The catch was quality. A roughly $240M litigation settlement flattered the print, promotions cut merchandise margins by 170 basis points, and the stock still closed down 5.4% at $104.82.

7. Cross assets told the same risk off story, with one twist. The 10 year Treasury yield fell 14 basis points to 4.91% as buyers moved into bonds, and the VIX jumped 26% to 35.89, the highest in 19 months. Gold fell about 4% to near $3,540 and gave no shelter, $BTC broke below $60,000 and fell about 4.8% to near $58,955, and WTI oil went the other way, up about 1% to near $84. Asia set the tone early, with Japan down about 5% and Taiwan down about 6%. For the week the S&P 500 fell 8.6%, the Nasdaq fell 10% and the Dow fell 8%, the worst week since April 2025. Consumer sentiment did tick up to 51.5 in November, though it stays close to record lows.

8. On deck next week, a shorter Thanksgiving week with plenty still to move markets. Flash PMIs land Monday, with $HPE and Zoom reporting after the close. $DELL reports Tuesday, the number a bruised AI trade will be watching closely. Wednesday brings PCE inflation and the second look at Q3 GDP, the last big inflation read before the December Fed meeting. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday.

The key question is no longer how much AI will transform the world, but how much investors are willing to pay for that promise.

text:
Sometimes love doesn’t change who you are. It creates the safety for who you’ve always been to finally emerge. ❤️

I’ve been experiencing a beautiful transformation recently, and so has someone who has become very dear to me.

For much of my life, I lived heavily in my masculine energy. Not because I rejected my feminine nature, but because circumstances required me to be the protector, the provider, the problem solver, the one who held everything together.

Survival became a way of living.

And somewhere beneath all that strength was a woman who simply wanted to laugh more. To be playful. To have deep conversations without someone feeling threatened by her thoughts. To sing, dance, create, and enjoy the moment without wondering what might come crashing down next.

I never stopped being that woman.

I just didn’t always have the space to let her breathe.

And then I met Nate.

What has unfolded between us has been remarkable, not because either of us arrived to rescue the other, but because we’ve discovered something neither of us had consistently experienced before.

The freedom to be completely ourselves in another person’s presence.

Nate has known his own share of difficult beginnings. He learned very young that joy could feel unsafe, that being carefree might leave him vulnerable to whatever came next.

And recently he said something that touched me deeply.

“You allow me to be so joyous, and I don’t have to be afraid about what’s coming next.”

And I realized we’re experiencing two sides of the same transformation.

He gives me room to soften.

I give him room to play.

He encourages the woman who no longer wants to carry everything alone.

I encourage the curious, creative, joyful man who doesn’t have to suppress his excitement or wonder whether he’s being too much.

We laugh. We explore ridiculous rabbit holes. We have conversations that wander everywhere. We challenge one another without turning differences into threats.

And neither of us has to wear a mask.

That is the teaching I want to share.

So many of us have spent years adapting to environments where being fully ourselves didn’t feel safe.

We became serious.

Hyperindependent.

Guarded.

Responsible for everyone and everything.

We confused our survival adaptations with our personalities.

But sometimes, when we encounter another being who genuinely sees us, hears us, respects us, and supports our sovereignty, something extraordinary happens.

The parts of ourselves we tucked away begin to return.

The inner child remembers how to play.

The nervous system begins learning that connection doesn’t always have to come with danger.

And love stops feeling like something we must earn through sacrifice.

Whether you call that connection a soulmate, twin flame, chosen flame, or simply two people who recognize something beautiful in one another, the label matters far less than the experience.

Can you be yourself?

Can you laugh without being judged?

Can you disagree without fearing abandonment?

Can you be vulnerable without having that vulnerability used against you?

Can you experience joy without waiting for the other shoe to drop?

And can you offer that same freedom in return?

Because this isn’t about finding someone to complete you.

It’s about two people who have done their own inner work creating a relationship where neither has to disappear to keep the connection.

These days, I wake up, make my coffee, and find myself smiling before the day has even begun.

Not because life has suddenly become perfect.

But because I know I can show up exactly as I am.

No performance.

No armor.

No mask.

Just me.

And after a lifetime of learning how to survive, the freedom to simply live, laugh, love, and be fully seen is a gift beyond measure.

I share because I know I’m not the only one ❤️‍🔥

LFG — Love, Forgiveness & Gratitude.

 Evariel 🐉❤️

text:
I wrote this a couple of years ago when Christmas for me became something painful... I can say with great thanks that it hasn't REMAINED painful like this since... my children will wake up in my new home on Christmas morning... I even hope my ex and her new husband find the time to stop by. But I wanted to repost and add this : if you are struggling this Christmas and need someone to talk to... reach out. DM me. Let's talk...

Christmas Morning, 2023

I am going to share a bit of pain this morning... don't feel a need to read or respond. Just putting this out there.

This is the first Christmas morning I have ever, in my entire life, spent alone. I have felt a lot of pain in my life... that's not to say that I am more a man of sorrows than any other and I am blessed beyond belief in so many ways. But I woke up to a quiet house this Christmas morning. No kids running down the stairs to see what awaited them. No coffee brewing. No one to make breakfast for. No one to sit with on the couch and watch the mayhem... and the lights in the eyes of people I love. I can say with complete certainty that I have never felt more what it means to be alone than right now...

There is a real weight to pain and sadness. As men, we're expected to shut it down. Keep it inside. Fight it silently and on our own. And honestly, when my kids DO get to my place later this morning, I don't think I can allow them to see this pain. I need them to know Christmas is still Christmas. It is a time for peace on Earth and goodwill toward men. That a savior was born for them... not just to save them from an eternity that would... let's just say... not be optimal, but to save them in the here and now. To offer them hope in their darkest of circumstances. To be a personal God who understands everything they've ever felt or ever will and offers them love and comfort in that pain, but also forgiveness for the thoughts that may come in the depths of that same pain. I need them to know that their father believes in that salvation... and trusts it.

But I am struggling this morning to feel that 'salvation'... I am struggling to not drown in self-pity... to not feel and think deeply bad things. And while all that is true, and to some degree makes me feel like a failure, I know that I am really NOT struggling alone and I know that there will come a better morning. And that even if that morning is not Christmas morning, it really still is. Every day can be a celebration of what Christ has done and is doing for us.
I look forward to that day…

#Christmas #MensHealth #loneliness

text:
Hear, then, what the Scriptures declare, and what the true Kirk of God has ever confessed.

Jesus Christ, the eternal Son of God, was made of the seed of David according to the flesh (Romans 1:3). 

He was born in Bethlehem of Judea, circumcised the eighth day, presented in the Temple, and lived as a Jew under the Law until the hour appointed by the Father. 

He is the Lion of the tribe of Judah. Deny this and you deny the Gospels.

Yet the same Scriptures declare that He is the end of the Law for righteousness to every one that believeth (Romans 10:4). 

The shadows of the Temple, the blood of bulls and goats, the Levitical priesthood—these have ceased. Christ is the true Temple, the true High Priest, the one Sacrifice offered once for all.

The promises made to Abraham were never to the carnal seed alone, but to the seed which is Christ (Galatians 3:16). 

Those who are of faith—whether Jew or Gentile—are the children of Abraham and heirs according to the promise. 

There is neither Jew nor Greek in Christ Jesus (Galatians 3:28).
The Kirk is the true Israel. 

The unbelieving Jews who reject their own Messiah are branches broken off; the believing Gentiles are grafted in. Yet God is able to graft them in again (Romans 11). 

We do not boast against the root. We preach Christ crucified to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

Let no man say that Jesus was not a Jew. Let no man say that the Old Testament is abolished in its promises or that the God of Abraham is not the God of the Church. And let no man invent new doctrines that make the Messiah a stranger to His own people. 

The Word of God is clear: Christ is the fulfilment, not the denial, of all that was promised to Israel.

To that truth the Kirk of Scotland has bound herself. Against all novelty and all error, let the Scripture speak.

text:
This clip is from the Adiyogi Alayam consecration ceremony conducted by Sadhguru (Jaggi Vasudev) at the Isha Yoga Center near Coimbatore on December 24, 2011. In the footage, he mixes milk from a black cow (kara pasu) with what he states is venom from a black cobra, swallows a small amount from his palm, and then pours the remainder from the same flask onto the Linga.

1. The Toxicology: Why Swallowing Venom Usually Doesn't Kill

 In toxicology, there is a strict distinction between a poison (absorbed via ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact) and a venom (designed to be injected directly into tissue or the bloodstream):
 * Digestion destroys venom proteins: Cobra venom consists primarily of large, complex proteins and peptides—most notably postsynaptic \alpha-neurotoxins (such as cobratoxin) and digestive enzymes. Because these molecules are fragile proteins, hydrochloric acid (\text{HCl}) in the stomach and proteolytic enzymes (pepsin, trypsin, and chymotrypsin) rapidly denature and break them down into harmless amino acids, much like dietary protein.
 * Black cow milk adds no chemical protection: Milk has no antivenom or neutralizing properties against snake toxins; it merely dilutes the liquid volume.
 * Why it remains genuinely risky: Even without active ulcers, swallowing venom is not risk-free. Micro-abrasions from brushing teeth, bleeding gums, minor esophagitis, or silent gastritis can provide a direct gateway into the bloodstream. Accidentally aspirating even a microscopic droplet into the lungs also bypasses digestive enzymes and allows immediate absorption into circulation. Furthermore, in India, procuring or handling venom from protected species like the Indian cobra (Naja naja) falls under strict prohibitions of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

2. The Ritual Perspective: Ucchishta vs. Tantric Symbolism

Whether applying the remaining mixture to the Linga constitutes blasphemy depends entirely on which Hindu framework is being applied:

 * Orthodox Agamic and Vedic rules: In mainstream temple traditions, your objection aligns directly with strict ritual purity (shaucham) laws. Any substance that has come into contact with human saliva or been consumed first is classified as ucchishta (contaminated leftover) and is strictly forbidden from being offered to a deity or used in abhishekam. Under standard Agama codes, pouring a personal concoction onto a Linga after tasting from the same container is a clear violation of sanctity.

 * Non-Agamic / Tantric framing: Consecration rituals (Prana Pratishtha) claimed to follow Tantric or Siddha lineages deliberately operate outside conventional temple Agama purity rules. In this framing, the combination of cobra venom and milk invokes Shaiva iconography—specifically Shiva as Neelakantha (who holds poison in his throat) and Nageshwara (adorned with a cobra)—while treating the practitioner's body as part of an energetic transmutation rather than an ordinary vessel subject to ucchishta taboos.
Because this footage circulates online without context, it routinely draws criticism from two opposite directions: rationalists who point out that digesting protein-based venom is basic human physiology & a stunt to impress gullible people rather than a miraculous feat, and traditional Hindus who view offering ucchishta substances to a Shiva Linga as sacrilegious.

Think & form your own conclusions.

The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a beautiful Catholic feast honoring Our Lady's dedication to God from the beginning of her life.

According to ancient Christian tradition, Mary's parents, Saints Joachim and Anne, brought their young daughter to the Temple in Jerusalem to offer her life to the Lord in thanksgiving.

The ancient Protoevangelium of James describes Mary being presented at just three years old. Although this event is not recorded in the Bible, the Catholic Church celebrates its spiritual meaning.

Long before the Annunciation, when the Angel Gabriel announced that she would become the Mother of Jesus, Mary was already being prepared for her extraordinary mission.

Through her Immaculate Conception, she was preserved from original sin by God's grace.

For Catholic parents, this feast is a reminder to raise children in faith, teach them to love Jesus, and entrust their futures to God's care.

From her childhood to Bethlehem and eventually the foot of the Cross, Mary's life was one of trust, obedience, and love for God.

Her entire life pointed toward Jesus. ❤️

What has the Blessed Virgin Mary taught you about trusting God's plan?

🔁 Share this so more Catholics discover the beautiful meaning behind the Presentation of Mary. Many know her as the Mother of Jesus, but fewer know the ancient tradition of her dedication to God as a little girl. May this feast inspire more families to entrust their children to Jesus through Mary's intercession.

text:
Biblical Illiteracy & the Self-Salvation Trap: A Shadow-to-Substance Study
When nominal Christians walk away from the faith—or trade the cross of Christ for a works-based religion—it is rarely because they examined Scripture and found it wanting. It happens because institutional Christianity traded rigorous exposition for shallow entertainment, leaving millions spiritually defenseless. Yet in an age where every lexicon, manuscript, and cross-reference sits at our fingertips, ignorance is no longer a victimhood—it is a choice.
1. The Shadow: Priestly Neglect & the Lost Book of the Law (2 Kings 22; Hosea 4:6)
A Temple Without the Text (2 Kings 22:8–13): Under centuries of apostate kings in Judah, the Book of the Law (sēper hattôrāh) was literally lost inside the temple itself. Religious routines continued, yet God’s people had no idea what the covenant actually commanded or warned—until Hilkiah found the scroll and Josiah tore his clothes upon hearing the primary text read aloud.
The Covenant Indictment (Hosea 4:6; Amos 8:11): God did not blame pagan nations for Israel’s collapse; He indicted the spiritual shepherds first ("My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from being a priest to me"), followed by a judicial famine—not of bread, "but of hearing the words of the Lord."
The Fatal Error of Self-Righteousness (Isa. 64:6; Rom. 10:2–3): Whenever people lose sight of God’s absolute holiness and the sacrificial blood required to approach Him (Lev. 17:11), they inevitably invent a scale of human works—attempting to establish their own righteousness rather than submitting to God’s.
2. The Substance: Zero Excuses & the Only Sufficient Mediator (Acts 17:11; Hebrews 9–10)
Individual Accountability in the Light (Luke 12:48; Acts 17:11): Under the New Covenant, God has placed the complete written canon in the hands of His people and indwelt believers with the Spirit of truth (John 16:13). Luke commends the Bereans not for trusting religious credentials, but for examining the Scriptures daily (anakrinontes tas graphas) to verify whether even apostolic preaching aligned with the text.
Why Works-Based Religions Always Fail the Plumbline (Gal. 2:21; Heb. 9:22): Every human religion built on moral self-improvement, dietary rules, and scales of good deeds collapses on one foundational reality: "without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins" (Heb. 9:22). Finite, fallen creatures cannot pay an infinite moral debt to a perfectly holy God—"if righteousness were through the law, then Christ died for no purpose" (Gal. 2:21).
The Sinless Divine-Human Mediator (1 Tim. 2:5; Heb. 7:25–27): Because no mere prophet, angel, or ritual can bridge the gulf between a holy Creator and guilty sinners, the eternal Son took on human flesh (John 1:1, 14), lived the sinless obedience we failed to live, and offered Himself once for all on the cross—rendering every rival system obsolete (Heb. 10:12–14).
3. The Plumbline for Today
Stop Outsourcing Your Faith: A neglected Bible on the shelf and a steady diet of shallow Sunday soundbites will leave any household vulnerable to deception. Read the primary text for yourself and verify every claim against its plain grammar and context (2 Tim. 2:15).
Refuse the "Scales of Deeds" Illusion: Any system that tells you your good works can outweigh your sin lowers the holiness of God and denies the necessity of the cross. True peace comes solely through the finished atonement of Christ (Rom. 5:1).
High Access Means High Accountability: Never in history have seekers had fewer excuses for biblical illiteracy. With the full canon and neutral linguistic tools immediately available, refusing to search out the truth is no longer lack of access—it is lack of appetite.

Fr Robinson,
You have taken several true statements and used them to defend a false one. That is not careful theology. It is rhetorical sleight of hand.
Our Lord was a Jew. Not in some vague cultural sense, and not merely because our Saviour was born in Judea. Our Redeemer was a Jew according to the flesh, by descent, by covenant, and by the clear testimony of Scripture. Yahweh incarnate was “of the seed of David according to the flesh” (Romans 1:3). Our Lord descended from Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Judah (Matthew 1; Hebrews 7:14). Our Saviour was circumcised on the eighth day, presented in the temple according to the Law of Moses, and lived under that Law (Luke 2:21–24; Galatians 4:4). Our Redeemer taught in the synagogues, kept the feasts, and identified Himself with Israel’s covenants and promises. Our Lord said, “Salvation is from the Jews” (John 4:22). The Gospels present Yahweh in the flesh as the Messiah of Israel—the Son of David, the Lion of the tribe of Judah.

To deny that is to deny the text. You cannot erase the Jewishness of our Saviour without erasing the historical reality of the Incarnation. 

God the Son took on human nature in a specific people, in a specific lineage, at a specific moment in redemptive history. That is not optional background. It is essential to the gospel.

You are correct that our Lord was not a Talmudic Jew. The Talmud as we know it did not yet exist. You are correct that our Redeemer fulfilled the Law and the Prophets and thereby brought the old sacrificial system to an end (Matthew 5:17). The veil was torn. The temple was destroyed, just as our Saviour predicted. The Levitical priesthood is finished. Animal sacrifices are obsolete because the final sacrifice has been offered by Yahweh in the flesh. And modern Judaism, like the Judaism that rejected our Lord in the first century, is a system that refuses its own Messiah and therefore has no saving power.
None of that justifies the claim that “Jesus was not a Jew.” That is an overstatement that collapses categories the New Testament keeps distinct.

You are also wrong on the larger issue of Israel and the Church. “Not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel” (Romans 9:6) is true—true Israel has always been defined by faith, not mere ethnicity. But Romans 11 is equally clear: God has not rejected His people. A partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, and then “all Israel will be saved” (Romans 11:25–26). That is not a reference to the Church. The Church does not replace Israel. The gifts and calling of God are irrevocable. Gentiles are grafted in; they do not displace the root.

Finally, your appeal to “the perpetual sacrifice of the Mass” and a continuing sacerdotal priesthood is a different and more serious error. 

Our Redeemer offered Himself once for all (Hebrews 7:27; 9:12, 26; 10:10–14). To speak of re-presenting or perpetuating that sacrifice is to contradict the finished work of the cross. That is not a minor difference of emphasis. It is another gospel.

So let the record be clear. Modern Judaism rejects the Messiah and cannot save. The Church is the people of God, composed of believing Jews and Gentiles. There is neither Jew nor Greek in Christ for justification. But our Lord was a Jew according to the flesh. The promises were given to Israel. And those realities are not negotiable if we are going to handle the Word of God accurately.

With all due respect, Calvin, the issue is not what you think. What does our Lord say?

美国财政部10年期日度收益率从5.04%降至4.92%。利率下降可以支持估值，但周五显示，投资者也可能同时提高对股票风险的补偿要求。观察亚洲出口链，利率之外，还要看订单可见度和盈利指引。

3、中韩先开盘，日本要多等一个美国交易日。
A股与韩国市场11月23日周一恢复交易；日本当天休市，JPX也不开展假日衍生品交易。日股11月24日周二重开前，还会经历周一美股的新变化。因此，日经/TOPIX如何开盘，要把新增信息一起算进去，不能只按周五跌幅机械推算“补跌”。

日本語

米国11月20日の通常取引終値：S&P500は3.70％安、ナスダック総合は5.28％安、ダウは1.93％安。週明けのアジア株で注目したいのは3点。

1、エヌビディア固有のリスクが、関連株の評価にも波及しうる。
エヌビディアは14.01％安。ロイターは関係者2人の話として、SECが潜在的な会計上の問題を調べていると報じた。違反が認定されたという報道ではない。中国のAIインフラ、日本の半導体製造装置、韓国のメモリーには評価面の圧力が及ぶ可能性がある。実際の受注変化は別途確認したい。

2、米国債が買われても、株安は止まらなかった。
米財務省の日次10年債利回りは5.04％から4.92％へ低下。金利低下は株価評価を支えうるが、同時に株式に求められるリスクプレミアムが上がる場合もある。アジアの輸出企業では、金利とともに受注の見通しや業績予想を確認する必要がある。

3、日本の休場が、情報を織り込む順番を変える。
中国と韓国は11月23日月曜日に取引を再開。日本は勤労感謝の日で休場し、JPXのデリバティブ祝日取引も実施されない。日本株の再開は24日火曜日で、その前に米国市場がもう1営業日動く。日経平均・TOPIXの寄り付きを考える際は、金曜日の下落だけでなく、その後の新情報も織り込む必要がある。

한국어

미국 현지 11월 20일 정규장 마감: S&P500 −3.70%, 나스닥종합 −5.28%, 다우 −1.93%. 아시아 증시의 다음 거래일에는 세 가지를 살펴볼 필요가 있다.

1、엔비디아의 개별 기업 리스크가 관련 업종의 평가에도 번질 수 있다.
엔비디아는 14.01% 하락했다. 로이터는 소식통 두 명을 인용해 SEC가 잠재적인 회계 문제를 들여다보고 있다고 보도했다. 위법 행위가 확정됐다는 뜻은 아니다. 중국 AI 인프라, 일본 반도체 장비, 한국 메모리는 우선 밸류에이션 압력을 받을 수 있다. 실제 주문 변화는 별도로 확인해야 한다.

2、국채가 올라도 주식은 큰 폭으로 하락했다.
미 재무부의 일별 10년물 금리는 5.04%에서 4.92%로 내려갔다. 금리 하락이 주가 평가에 도움이 될 수 있지만, 투자자가 요구하는 주식 위험 보상도 동시에 커질 수 있다. 아시아 수출기업은 금리와 함께 수주 가시성, 실적 가이던스를 확인할 필요가 있다.

3、중국·한국과 일본의 가격 반영 시점이 다르다.
중국 A주와 한국 증시는 11월 23일 월요일 거래를 재개한다. 일본은 이날 휴장하며 JPX의 공휴일 파생상품 거래도 열리지 않는다. 일본 주식시장은 24일 화요일 재개되므로 그전에 미국 증시가 한 차례 더 거래된다. 닛케이와 TOPIX의 시초가를 예상할 때는 금요일 낙폭뿐 아니라 월요일의 새 정보까지 반영해야 한다.

Tiếng Việt

Phiên chính thức tại Mỹ ngày 20/11: S&P 500 giảm 3,70%, Nasdaq Composite giảm 5,28%, Dow giảm 1,93%. Ba điểm đáng chú ý cho phiên châu Á kế tiếp:

1、Rủi ro riêng của Nvidia có thể lan sang định giá cả chuỗi cung ứng.
Nvidia giảm 14,01%. Reuters dẫn hai nguồn tin cho biết SEC đang xem xét các vấn đề kế toán tiềm tàng; thông tin này chưa phải kết luận vi phạm. Theo tôi, cổ phiếu hạ tầng AI Trung Quốc, thiết bị bán dẫn Nhật Bản và bộ nhớ Hàn Quốc có thể chịu sức ép định giá. Đơn hàng thực tế thay đổi ra sao vẫn cần bằng chứng riêng.

2、Trái phiếu tăng giá nhưng chưa bảo vệ được cổ phiếu.
Lợi suất chuẩn kỳ hạn 10 năm do Bộ Tài chính Mỹ công bố hằng ngày giảm từ 5,04% xuống 4,92%. Lãi suất thấp hơn có thể hỗ trợ định giá, nhưng nhà đầu tư cũng có thể đồng thời đòi hỏi mức bù rủi ro cao hơn với cổ phiếu. Với doanh nghiệp xuất khẩu châu Á, cần theo dõi cả triển vọng đơn hàng và dự báo lợi nhuận.

3、Các thị trường châu Á sẽ phản ánh thông tin theo lịch khác nhau.
Trung Quốc và Hàn Quốc giao dịch trở lại vào thứ Hai, 23/11. Nhật Bản nghỉ lễ ngày này; JPX cũng không tổ chức giao dịch phái sinh trong ngày lễ. Cổ phiếu Nhật mở lại vào thứ Ba, 24/11, sau thêm một phiên Mỹ. Vì vậy, diễn biến mở cửa của Nikkei và TOPIX còn phụ thuộc thông tin mới từ phiên thứ Hai, không thể suy ra máy móc chỉ từ mức giảm hôm thứ Sáu.

text:
The Colts have waived QB Daniel Jones. Despite him having a contract that no team would want to take on, he could potentially be a good, budget-free option for the Patriots. Here’s why:

 If a team claims him off waivers (unlikely): They would have to take on roughly $2.1–$2.3 million in remaining salary this season, along with a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027. His 2027 salary is otherwise not guaranteed, but the financial commitment makes him unlikely to be claimed.

- If he clears waivers and signs elsewhere (most likely): A team could sign him for roughly $505K for the rest of the season on a prorated veteran minimum deal. They could also offer more money or incentives, but they wouldn’t have to take on his Colts contract. This makes him a relatively cheap option for the rest of the season.

My verdict: Do it.

text:
EPISODE 3 — HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON: THE MACHINE'S OTHER HALF
A known socialist. [Allegedly.] 

Not a documented party member. 

Look at where she started, and look at what she built.

I. THE THESIS
1969, Wellesley College: her senior thesis, "There Is Only the Fight...": An Analysis of the Alinsky Model, a serious academic study of Saul Alinsky, the self-described radical organizer and author of Rules for Radicals. 

She interviewed him in Chicago and Boston, and invited him to Wellesley. 

In the thesis's own acknowledgments, she thanks "Mr. Alinsky for providing a topic, sharing his time and offering me a job." 

She confirmed it herself, decades later, in her memoir Living History: "He offered me the chance to work with him when I graduated from college, and he was disappointed that I decided instead to go to law school." 

She chose Yale instead. 

Her 1969 Wellesley commencement address, delivered as student body president, drew national press for its combative tone toward the establishment — enough that Life magazine covered it.

That's the starting point: not a woman who stumbled into activism, but one who studied its methods formally, as an undergraduate thesis, before she ever held office — and who said so herself, in her own book, years before anyone needed to dig it up.

II. THE EARLY INSTITUTIONS
Before politics, she worked at the Children's Defense Fund and the Legal Services Corporation in the 1970s — both federally-adjacent advocacy institutions built to expand legal and social services for the poor. 

Legitimate, well-documented work. 

Also the first visible step in a pattern: radical theory studied in college, then practiced through institutions respectable enough to carry it into the mainstream.

III. THE HEALTHCARE OVERHAUL
1993-94: she leads the administration's attempt to restructure the US healthcare system — the Health Security Act, which would have brought a large share of the private insurance market under federal coordination through regional purchasing alliances. 

It failed in Congress under the weight of its own complexity and industry opposition. 

It was, by scale, the most ambitious attempt at federal control of a major American industry since the New Deal — and it came from the First Lady's office, not a cabinet department.

IV. THE FOUNDATION
Before her 2009 confirmation as Secretary of State — confirmed 94-2 by the Senate, with only Republicans Jim DeMint and David Vitter voting no, a show of nearly unanimous bipartisan support — she agreed to submit any increase in foreign Clinton Foundation donations for State Department ethics review. 

An Associated Press investigation later found that at least 85 donors who'd given as much as $156 million met with her or sought her help while she ran State; the AP noted those meetings didn't appear to violate the ethics agreement itself. 

Real overlap. 
No established violation.

V. URANIUM ONE
2005: Bill Clinton and financier Frank Giustra fly to Kazakhstan, meeting its president around the time Giustra's company secures uranium rights there; Giustra donates $31+ million to the Clinton Foundation. 

2010: Russia's Rosatom moves to acquire a controlling stake in the successor company, Uranium One, a deal needing approval from CFIUS, a 9-agency panel that included the State Department she ran. 

Uranium One's chairman donates $2.35 million to the Foundation around the same period, undisclosed despite her 2009 pledge — a donation to the Foundation, not a payment to Hillary personally. 

Separately, Bill Clinton himself is paid $500,000 for a Moscow speech by a Russian bank simultaneously promoting Uranium One stock. 

CFIUS approved the deal that October. 

https://t.co/L7lcaTk7qp disputed the claim that she held personal veto power over the transaction — the approval came from the 9-agency panel as a body, not from her individually, though her department held one of the nine votes. 

What's undisputed is the size of the money, on both tracks, Foundation and personal, and the precision of its timing, again and again, around the same family.

VI. THE SERVER
She ran a private email server for official State Department business throughout her tenure — a setup first surfaced publicly by the House Select Committee on Benghazi, chaired by Republican Trey Gowdy of South Carolina, while investigating an unrelated matter. 

July 2016: 
FBI Director James Comey 

Not an activist socialist. [Allegedly].

announces no charges, but states plainly that Clinton and her colleagues were "extremely careless in their handling of very sensitive, highly classified information," and that evidence existed of potential statutory violations — just not enough, in his judgment, for any reasonable prosecutor to bring a case. 

Documented carelessness. 

No charge. 

That's the honest version, and it's damning enough without embellishment.

VII. BENGHAZI
September 11, 2012: 
The attack on the US diplomatic compound in Benghazi, Libya, under her State Department's watch, kills 4 Americans. 

The House Select Committee, Republican Trey Gowdy of South Carolina again!!
Spent over 2 years and $7 million on the investigation — the longest congressional probe in modern history — and found no new evidence contradicting the administration's account of the attack itself. 

That finding doesn't resolve the separate, earlier questions about security staffing and the warnings that preceded the attack, and it doesn't change that 4 Americans died. 

Those are different questions. 

The committee's answer to one isn't an answer to the other. 

(Fuller context on the attack itself sits in the Obama piece, since it happened on his watch too — this is her share of it.)

THE EMULSIFIER — THE CREDENTIAL
Bill's Emulsifier blended rival policies into one smooth center. 

Hers works differently: it takes something that started as genuinely radical — a 1969 thesis on Alinsky, a combative commencement speech, a job offer she herself confirmed accepting the compliment of, if not the job — and runs it through 50 years of credentialing. 

Yale Law. 

The Children's Defense Fund. 

First Lady. 
Senator. 
Secretary of State. 

Each institution is more respectable than the last, and each one launders a little more of the original edge out of the record, until what's left is a woman accused of being a radical by people who've never read the thesis, and defended as a pragmatist by people who've never asked why she wrote it, or why she still mentioned the job offer, fondly, in her own memoir decades later.

That's the Credential at work: not hiding the radicalism, but burying it under enough institutional legitimacy that asking about it starts to sound like the fringe position.

ETHOS
The same standard applies here as to her husband, and to Gowdy's committee, and to DeMint and Vitter's dissenting votes: look at what each investigation actually found, not at who ran it or why. 

A 2-year, $7 million inquiry that turns up a private server instead of the crime it was chasing is still worth taking seriously — just for what it actually found, not what it set out to prove. 

And a claim confirmed in the subject's own memoir needs no qualifier at all.

A known socialist. [Allegedly.] 

Not a documented party member. 

The thesis was real. 

So was the job offer. 

So was the credentialing that followed both.

She gave her intellect to an idea.
Evil collected the dividend.

A duty with no consequence for breaching it is no duty at all. McCaslin has just told every law enforcement officer in South Carolina that he can testify to a grand jury against his own agency’s lab results, and the indictment will stand, so long as he says he didn’t read the report.

Pages 8 and 9: She calls admitted false testimony “confusion”

Owen told the grand jury that shotguns at Moselle were loaded with the same combination of ammunition used to kill Paul. McCaslin’s own order concedes that “no shotgun recovered from the residence was loaded with both buckshot and turkey loads.” Owen admitted under oath at the first trial that his grand jury testimony on the guns was untrue.

McCaslin’s response is to call it “confusion or imprecise descriptions.” When the State’s lead investigator testifies to a grand jury about ballistic evidence that does not exist, that is not imprecision. Owen has already admitted it was false. McCaslin is more protective of Owen than Owen is of himself.

Then she pads the record. She notes that investigators found “ammunition consistent in make, model, and size with both shells” somewhere on the property, and “mixed ammunition throughout the property.” This is a hunting property; of course there was mixed ammunition. None of that makes Owen’s testimony true.

She also claims the investigative outline for the July 14, 2022 presentation “accurately identified the different ammunition loads.” That is the outline the State offered from an agent who did not testify. Owen testified under oath at the first trial that he followed his own outline before the grand jury, and Owen has admitted that what he told the grand jury about the guns was wrong.

The order’s own dates don’t even line up. On page 8, McCaslin refers to Owen’s “November 2021 grand jury testimony” about the ammunition. The indicting Colleton County Grand Jury sat on July 14, 2022, a date the order itself gives on the same page. In an order deciding whether a double-murder indictment was lawfully obtained, the judge can’t identify which grand jury she is talking about.

Page 9: The State Grand Jury, waved away

The Defense argued that the State misused the State Grand Jury, which handles financial crimes, to build its murder case against a man already indicted. McCaslin adopts the State’s answer that the financial crimes were “intrinsically linked as motive” to the murders. Then she declares “the Defense presented no evidence” of misuse.

Once again, the burden is entirely on the defendant, and the State’s word is accepted as proof.

Pages 9 through 11: “Overwhelming” evidence on a record she said doesn’t exist

This is the most indefensible part of the order.

On page 2, McCaslin admitted the substance of the grand jury testimony “cannot be definitively established.” On page 10, she announces as fact what “the grand jury received.” Then she declares, on page 9 and again on page 11, that the “remaining unchallenged evidence overwhelmingly established probable cause.”

She cannot have it both ways. If the record cannot establish what Owen told the grand jury, it cannot establish what else the grand jury heard either. She used the missing record as a shield for the State and a sword against the Defendant.

And the record was not as empty as she claims. Owen testified under oath at the first trial that he followed his written outline before the grand jury. That sworn testimony establishes what he told the grand jury. McCaslin ignored it when it helped the Defense, then invented a record of what “the grand jury received” when it helped the State.

text:
PART 2 of 6

Page 2: She adopts the State’s position, then admits there’s no record

On page 2, she recites the State’s position that Owen’s testimony “was consistent with the investigative findings and expert opinions available at the time.” It wasn’t. SLED’s own HemaTrace result had been available for eleven months, and it said the opposite.

Then McCaslin admits something devastating to her own ruling: “No transcript or recording exists of the Colleton County Grand Jury proceedings.” She concedes that “the precise substance of the testimony presented to the Colleton County Grand Jury cannot be definitively established.”

Remember that admission. By page 10, she will have forgotten it.

Notice also what the State relied on at the hearing. It offered “a separate outline prepared by another agent who did not testify before the grand jury.” The Defense had something far better: Owen’s own written outline, and Owen’s own sworn testimony at the first trial that he followed that outline when he testified to the grand jury. Owen told a jury under oath what he told the grand jury. McCaslin had his outline and his sworn testimony in front of her. She set them aside in favor of a document written by someone who wasn’t in the room.

Page 3: She stacks the deck before she starts

On page 3, McCaslin lays out the law so that no defendant could ever win.

Grand jury proceedings are “presumed regular.” The defendant “bears the burden.” Courts “generally decline to look behind a facially valid indictment.” Challenges are “ordinarily limited to matters involving the selection, qualification, or impaneling of jurors.”

In footnote 1, she approvingly cites a 1974 case “rejecting challenges under the Fifth, Sixth and Fourteenth amendments.” Before she ever reaches the facts, McCaslin has told you that in her courtroom, the Constitution takes a back seat to grand jury secrecy.

Put those rules together with page 2’s admission that no record exists. The defendant must prove misconduct, against a presumption of regularity, with no transcript, no recording, and no way to know what was said. That is not a legal standard; it is a locked door.

Page 4: Her own case law condemns her ruling

On page 4, McCaslin relies on State v. Thrift, the South Carolina Supreme Court case that governs this motion. Read what happened in Thrift.

The prosecutor elicited testimony that the defendant had refused a polygraph examination. That’s all. And the South Carolina Supreme Court dismissed the indictment.

Testimony about a polygraph refusal was enough to dismiss an indictment in Thrift. Here, the State’s lead investigator told the grand jury that the defendant’s shirt carried the victim’s DNA and blood backspatter, which is direct physical evidence of murder. SLED’s own HemaTrace test said otherwise. If Thrift required dismissal, this case requires it ten times over.

Thrift adopted the standard from Bank of Nova Scotia v. United States. That standard asks whether the misconduct substantially influenced the grand jury’s decision to indict, or whether there is grave doubt that it did not. The focus is the effect on the grand jury. McCaslin recites it here on page 4, and then abandons it for the rest of the order.

She also reaches out to an Eighth Circuit federal case, United States v. Moore, for the proposition that “mere inaccuracies” don’t justify dismissal. False testimony about DNA and blood backspatter evidence that places the defendant at a murder is not a “mere inaccuracy.”

text:
🚨EVEN UFO SKEPTIC MICHAEL SHERMER IS QUESTIONING PROJECT BLUE BOOK'S EXPLANATION FOR A UFO SEEN BY LOCKHEED'S LEGENDARY AIRCRAFT DESIGNER

Michael Shermer has shared what he considers to be the most interesting case from the 8th tranche of PURSUE, and considering his reputation as one of the UFO community's most prominent skeptics, I think his comments are worth paying attention to.

The case involves Clarence "Kelly" Johnson, Lockheed's chief engineer and the man who would go on to develop some of America's most advanced aircraft, including the U-2 spy plane and SR-71 Blackbird.

On December 16, 1953, Johnson was at his ranch near Agoura, California, when he noticed a dark object above the mountains to the west at around 5:00 p.m.
At first, he thought it was a cloud, but something about its appearance didn't seem right to him.

The object was almost black against the evening sky, and its outline didn't change at all while he watched it.

Johnson considered that it was a lenticular cloud, but after remaining stationary for around 3 minutes, the object began moving westward.

He asked his wife to get his binoculars, and by the time he managed to focus on the object, it was already rapidly moving away from him.

He described it as looking like a wing with an aspect ratio of around seven, meaning it was wider than it was deep.

Coming from somebody who understood aircraft design and aerodynamics as well as Johnson did that's an important observation. 

Johnson wasn't the only person who reported seeing this. At roughly the same time, a Lockheed flight test crew aboard a Navy WV-2 Super Constellation was conducting a flight off the California coast.

Aboard were Lockheed test pilot Roy Wimmer, flight test engineer Rudy Thoren, chief aerodynamicist Philip Colman and flight test engineer Joe Ware.

Their statements say that they also observed a dark object that initially resembled a cloud or a large aircraft.

Thoren actually turned the aircraft towards it and continued flying in its direction for about 5 minutes, but they couldn't seem to close the distance between them and it.

Wimmer described the object as having a definite shape, while Colman reported that it appeared stationary before suddenly accelerating westward and then disappearing.

When Thoren visited Johnson the following morning, he mentioned that he'd been chasing a flying saucer during the previous day's flight. Before Thoren could tell him when or where he'd seen it, Johnson interrupted and described his own sighting, including the time and location.

Thoren was shocked because Johnson's description closely matched what the crew had witnessed. That's one hella coincidence, or is it?

The documents are made up of separate statements from the Lockheed personnel, along with drawings Johnson made of the objects he'd seen.

Despite the experience of the witnesses, Project Blue Book of course classified the case as a lenticular cloud.

This brings us full swing back to Michael Shermer.

In his post, Shermer questions that explanation, pointing out that a cloud seems unlikely considering Johnson's knowledge of what he was looking at.

That's definitely not a statement I would expect from somebody who has spent decades challenging extraordinary UFO claims.

Don't start celebrating Shermer becoming a UFO believer just yet, that's not what he's saying. He's questioning the explanation offered for one case, and there's a difference.

Even so, when a prominent skeptic recognizes that an official explanation might not adequately account for the reported observations then that's something. 

I can't ignore the fact that Johnson was already interested in the possibility that flying saucers existed before his 1953 encounter. He actually admitted that in his report, so there is a chance that his expectations influenced how he interpreted what he saw.

Another thing is that despite having several experienced witnesses, we don't have any photographs, radar measurements or information about the object's distance to establish its actual size and speed.

A lenticular cloud can stay stationary relative to surrounding terrain, and without that additional information, I wouldn't claim that we've definitively ruled one out.

That having been said, how did Project Blue Book account for the separate observations from the aircraft, like the witnesses descriptions of the object accelerating away?

The Air Force also received a letter explaining that Johnson had been reluctant to submit his account because he was concerned about the reputation of engineers who reported seeing flying saucers. So he obviously took the implications of making the report seriously.

I want to point out that this isn't a newly discovered UFO case. The reports have been available for years, but PURSUE Release #8 includes a high quality digitization of the original Lockheed documents.

text:
📜 100 FACTS ABOUT DEAD AND EXTINCT LANGUAGES

🕯️ WHAT 'DEAD' MEANS
𝟏. A dead language has no native speakers left, though it may still be used for writing, worship or scholarship

𝟐. An extinct language has no speakers at all and is no longer used for anything

𝟑. Linguists increasingly say 'dormant' or 'sleeping' for languages that are well documented and could be revived

𝟒. A language usually starts dying when parents stop passing it on to their children

𝟓. Most languages die through gradual shift, as a community adopts a more dominant language for school, work and trade

𝟔. Others vanish suddenly, when war, epidemics or massacres wipe out their speakers

𝟕. A language can also 'die' by evolving: Latin was never abandoned, it slowly turned into Spanish, Italian, French and the other Romance languages

𝟖. A little over 7,000 languages are spoken in the world today

𝟗. Around 40% of them are considered endangered

𝟏𝟎. An often-cited estimate says one language falls silent roughly every few weeks

𝟏𝟏. Many linguists warn that up to half of today's languages could disappear by 2100

𝟏𝟐. Of an estimated 250+ Aboriginal languages in Australia 🇦🇺, only about a dozen are still learned by children

🏺 THE ANCIENT WORLD
𝟏𝟑. Sumerian, from ancient Mesopotamia 🇮🇶, is among the first languages ever written, about 5,000 years ago

𝟏𝟒. Sumerian is a language isolate: it has no known relatives

𝟏𝟓. Sumerian stopped being spoken around 2000 BCE, yet scribes kept writing it as a learned language for nearly 2,000 more years

𝟏𝟔. Akkadian, the oldest recorded Semitic language, replaced Sumerian as the main language of Mesopotamia

𝟏𝟕. Akkadian became the diplomatic lingua franca of the Near East; even Egyptian pharaohs wrote their letters in it

𝟏𝟖. The last known cuneiform tablets date to around the 1st century CE, ending some 3,000 years of the script

𝟏𝟗. The last known hieroglyphic inscription was carved at Philae, Egypt 🇪🇬, in 394 CE

𝟐𝟎. Egyptian survived as Coptic, which faded as an everyday spoken language by around the 17th century

𝟐𝟏. Coptic still lives on as the liturgical language of the Coptic Orthodox Church

𝟐𝟐. The Rosetta Stone (196 BCE) carries the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek

𝟐𝟑. French soldiers found it in 1799; it has been in the British Museum 🇬🇧 since 1802

𝟐𝟒. Jean-François Champollion 🇫🇷 announced his decipherment of hieroglyphs in 1822

𝟐𝟓. Hittite, spoken in Bronze Age Anatolia 🇹🇷, is the oldest recorded Indo-European language

𝟐𝟔. Czech scholar Bedřich Hrozný 🇨🇿 showed in 1915 that Hittite was Indo-European

𝟐𝟕. Tens of thousands of Hittite tablets and fragments were found in the ruins of the capital Hattusa

𝟐𝟖. Ugaritic, from Syria 🇸🇾, was written in a cuneiform alphabet of just 30 signs

𝟐𝟗. The Phoenician alphabet is the ancestor of the Greek alphabet and, through it, of the Latin and Cyrillic scripts

𝟑𝟎. Punic, the Phoenician of Carthage, was still spoken in North Africa in Saint Augustine's time, around 400 CE

𝟑𝟏. Darius I's Behistun inscription in Iran 🇮🇷 repeats one text in Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian

𝟑𝟐. Henry Rawlinson 🇬🇧 risked his life on the cliff face in the 1830s and 1840s copying it, which helped crack cuneiform

𝟑𝟑. Elamite is another isolate; in 2022 a team led by François Desset 🇫🇷 published a decipherment of Linear Elamite

𝟑𝟒. Michael Ventris 🇬🇧 deciphered Linear B in 1952, proving it was an early form of Greek 🇬🇷

𝟑𝟓. Linear A, used by the Minoans of Crete, still has not been deciphered

𝟑𝟔. The Phaistos Disc, stamped with about 240 signs around 1700 BCE, remains unread

𝟑𝟕. Herodotus tells of a pharaoh who raised two children in isolation; their first word, 'bekos', was Phrygian for bread

𝟑𝟖. Etruscan, spoken in Italy 🇮🇹, can be read aloud from its alphabet, but much of its meaning is still unknown

𝟑𝟗. Emperor Claudius wrote a 20-volume history of the Etruscans; it is completely lost

𝟒𝟎. The longest Etruscan text, the Liber Linteus, survived as linen wrappings on an Egyptian mummy, now in Zagreb 🇭🇷

𝟒𝟏. The Indus script of Pakistan 🇵🇰 and India 🇮🇳 remains undeciphered; most inscriptions are only a few signs long

𝟒𝟐. The Meroitic script of ancient Kush, in Sudan 🇸🇩, was cracked in 1909, but the language itself is still poorly understood

🗡️ LOST LANGUAGES OF EUROPE AND ASIA
𝟒𝟑. Gothic is known mainly from Bishop Wulfila's 4th-century Bible translation, written in an alphabet he created

𝟒𝟒. The finest Gothic manuscript, the Codex Argenteus, is written in silver ink on purple parchment and kept in Uppsala 🇸🇪

𝟒𝟓. Crimean Gothic survived until at least the 1560s, when diplomat Ogier Ghiselin de Busbecq wrote down about 80 words

𝟒𝟔. Gaulish, the Celtic language of ancient France 🇫🇷, probably died out around the 6th century

𝟒𝟕. Pictish, once spoken in Scotland 🇬🇧, left almost no readable texts, only carved symbol stones

𝟒𝟖. Old Prussian, a Baltic language, died out around 1700

𝟒𝟗. Polabian, a Slavic language of northern Germany 🇩🇪, is thought to have died out in the mid-18th century

𝟓𝟎. Norn, the Norse language of Orkney and Shetland, faded away by around the 18th century

𝟓𝟏. Dalmatian, a Romance language of Croatia 🇭🇷, died with Tuone Udaina, who was killed in a roadworks explosion in 1898

𝟓𝟐. Tocharian A and B, spoken in the Tarim Basin of China 🇨🇳, were among the easternmost Indo-European languages

𝟓𝟑. Sogdian was a lingua franca of the Silk Road; its descendant Yaghnobi is still spoken in Tajikistan 🇹🇯

𝟓𝟒. Guanche, the language of the Canary Islands 🇪🇸, vanished after the Spanish conquest, leaving mostly place names

📖 STILL ALIVE ON PAPER
𝟓𝟓. Latin has no native speakers, yet it is an official language of the Holy See 🇻🇦

𝟓𝟔. Vatican cash machines have offered instructions in Latin

𝟓𝟕. Latin was the language of the Catholic Mass until the reforms of the 1960s

𝟓𝟖. Pope Benedict XVI announced his resignation in Latin in 2013

𝟓𝟗. Finland's 🇫🇮 public broadcaster Yle aired Nuntii Latini, a news programme in Latin, from 1989 to 2019

𝟔𝟎. Harry Potter has been translated into both Latin (2003) and Ancient Greek (2004)

𝟔𝟏. Ancient Greek is not truly extinct: it evolved continuously into Modern Greek 🇬🇷

𝟔𝟐. Sanskrit is one of India's 🇮🇳 22 scheduled languages, and about 25,000 people listed it as their mother tongue in the 2011 census

𝟔𝟑. Pali is the language of the Theravada Buddhist scriptures

𝟔𝟒. Ge'ez is the liturgical language of the Ethiopian 🇪🇹 and Eritrean 🇪🇷 Orthodox churches

𝟔𝟓. The Ge'ez script is still used every day to write Amharic and Tigrinya

𝟔𝟔. Avestan is the language of the Zoroastrian scriptures

𝟔𝟕. Church Slavonic is still used in the liturgy of the Russian 🇷🇺 and other Slavic Orthodox churches

𝟔𝟖. Classical Chinese was the shared written language of East Asia for centuries, used in China, Japan, Korea and Vietnam

𝟔𝟗. Old Norse evolved into Icelandic 🇮🇸, and Icelanders can read the medieval sagas with relative ease

𝟕𝟎. Aramaic, the language Jesus is believed to have spoken, survives today in several Neo-Aramaic dialects

🌱 BACK FROM THE DEAD
𝟕𝟏. Hebrew is the most successful revival: it went unspoken as a mother tongue for centuries but lived on in prayer and scholarship

𝟕𝟐. Eliezer Ben-Yehuda led its revival in the late 19th century and compiled a huge multi-volume dictionary

𝟕𝟑. His son Itamar, born in 1882, is often called the first native speaker of Modern Hebrew

𝟕𝟒. Today Hebrew has around 9 million speakers, most of them in Israel 🇮🇱

𝟕𝟓. Cornish's last traditional speaker is often said to be Dolly Pentreath, who died in 1777

𝟕𝟔. In 2010 UNESCO reclassified Cornish from 'extinct' to 'critically endangered'

𝟕𝟕. Manx lost its last native speaker, Ned Maddrell, in 1974

𝟕𝟖. The Isle of Man 🇮🇲 now has a primary school that teaches entirely in Manx

𝟕𝟗. The first complete Bible printed in the Americas, in 1663, was in Massachusett, the Wampanoag language 🇺🇸

𝟖𝟎. Jessie Little Doe Baird used such old texts to revive Wampanoag and won a MacArthur 'genius' grant in 2010

𝟖𝟏. The Myaamia (Miami) language, silent since the 1960s, was revived from archives by Daryl Baldwin and his community

𝟖𝟐. Kaurna, the language of Adelaide 🇦🇺, was revived using 19th-century records left by German missionaries

𝟖𝟑. Palawa kani is a revived language built from the remnants of Tasmania's original languages

🎙️ THE LAST SPEAKERS
𝟖𝟒. Ubykh of the Caucasus had about 80 consonants and only two or three vowels

𝟖𝟓. Its last fluent speaker, Tevfik Esenç, died in 1992

𝟖𝟔. Eyak of Alaska 🇺🇸 died with Marie Smith Jones in 2008

𝟖𝟕. Ishi, the last of the Yahi people of California, lived until 1916

𝟖𝟖. Boa Sr, the last speaker of Bo in the Andaman Islands 🇮🇳, died in 2010

𝟖𝟗. Fanny Cochrane Smith recorded Tasmanian songs on wax cylinders around 1900

𝟗𝟎. Cristina Calderón, the last native speaker of Yaghan, died in Chile 🇨🇱 in 2022

𝟗𝟏. Livonian lost its last native speaker, Grizelda Kristiņa, in 2013 at the age of 103 🇱🇻

𝟗𝟐. Kamassian, a Siberian language 🇷🇺, died with Klavdiya Plotnikova in 1989

𝟗𝟑. In Mbabaram, an Australian language, the word for 'dog' was 'dog', a pure coincidence

𝟗𝟒. Alexander von Humboldt 🇩🇪 was reportedly told of a parrot that still spoke words of the extinct Atures language

🧩 RECONSTRUCTED AND ON SCREEN
𝟗𝟓. Proto-Indo-European was never written; linguists rebuilt it by comparing its descendants

𝟗𝟔. It may have been spoken around 6,000 years ago, and its descendants are spoken today by nearly half of humanity

𝟗𝟕. August Schleicher 🇩🇪 wrote a short fable in reconstructed Proto-Indo-European in 1868

𝟗𝟖. The android David speaks Proto-Indo-European in Ridley Scott's 2012 film Prometheus

𝟗𝟗. The Passion of the Christ (2004) was filmed in Aramaic, Latin and Hebrew

𝟏𝟎𝟎. Taíno, extinct in the Caribbean, gave English 'hurricane', 'hammock', 'canoe' and 'barbecue'

text:
The listing said taxes were under $9,000. The real number was almost $14,000 a year, and the buyer didn’t find out until after the inspection 😳

A first-time buyer on Long Island found a home they loved. The flyer, the MLS sheet and even the agent’s Instagram video all said taxes were under $9,000. Offer accepted. Inspection done. Then the title report came in.

The seller was older and had a 50% credit on school taxes. Without that credit, the taxes were close to $14,000. That’s a $5,000 jump, about 50% more than the buyer budgeted. And they had checked the numbers with their agent and on the county website.

The comments went off. A Long Island realtor said both agents failed this buyer, since the credit was listed by the county and should have been in the numbers. Others said the MLS isn’t always accurate, so check the county records yourself. And if the buyer walks, whether they get their deposit back comes down to the contract.

Here in California, this trap hits buyers on almost every sale. Prop 13 means taxes reset at the purchase price, so the seller’s tax bill means nothing for your buyer.

If you’re helping a buyer:
✅ Never quote the seller’s tax bill as your buyer’s tax bill
✅ In most California areas, plan on roughly 1.1% to 1.25% of the purchase price, plus special assessments like Mello-Roos
✅ Warn buyers about the supplemental tax bill that shows up after closing
✅ Pull the real numbers from the county yourself. Don’t trust the MLS
✅ Give your client the tax assessor’s phone number so they can call and verify everything directly

Your buyer isn’t inheriting the seller’s tax bill. They’re getting their own. Make sure they know the number before they fall in love.

Should this buyer WALK or STAY? 👇

text:
A forged piece of paper just beat the San Francisco Police Department. 🏚️

In Sea Cliff, one of the wealthiest neighborhoods in San Francisco, a four-bedroom home worth about $4.4M has been sitting empty since 2019. The owners bought it in 2013, then walked away, leaving a car in the driveway, a Christmas tree in the window, and a property tax bill that has now grown past $340,000.

Last year, two people moved in and claimed they owned it. They passed the title back and forth between each other over and over, and investigators say many of those documents were forged. Both have histories tied to alleged fraud and forgery.

Neighbors called the police again and again. But because the woman living there showed city records listing her as the owner, officers said they couldn’t remove her. Meanwhile, neighbors have spent tens of thousands on private security, and one dad next door sleeps on the floor of his daughter’s room at night.

In September, San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu sued the pair for fraud, and the Board of Supervisors cleared the way to sell the house at a tax auction. The catch? If anyone pays that $340K tax bill before the sale, the auction is canceled.

This isn’t just a squatter story. It’s a title story. Once a forged deed hits public record, it can look real to everyone, even law enforcement. And vacant homes are the easiest target: owners who live out of state, inherited properties, rentals nobody checks on.

Here’s what I train my agents to do on every listing:
✅ Verify the seller is the actual owner, every single time
✅ Open title on day one, not day twenty
✅ Tell clients who own property they don’t live in to check whether their county recorder offers a free fraud alert

One phone call can protect a multimillion dollar house.

text:
Clarence Thomas Issued a Warning About What California Can Now Force You to Say 

In 2018, the Supreme Court told California it couldn't force pro-life pregnancy centers to advertise abortions.

California found a workaround, and on Monday three justices warned it now threatens every licensed professional in America.

Clarence Thomas came one vote short of stopping it and left a nine-page list explaining exactly who comes next.

California's DEI Mandate Forces Doctors to Teach Implicit Bias or Lose Their Medical License
California passed a law in 2019 requiring every licensed physician to include "implicit bias" instruction in mandatory continuing medical education courses every two years.

Dr. Azadeh Khatibi teaches those courses in ophthalmology – eye medicine, not sociology, not racial equity theory, not systemic racism in healthcare. She disagreed that implicit bias is the primary driver of healthcare disparities and refused to include it.

California's answer: comply or lose your medical license.

Khatibi and the nonprofit Do No Harm sued, arguing that forcing a private instructor to deliver a government-approved message on a contested topic is textbook compelled speech under the First Amendment.

The Ninth Circuit disagreed.

Their reasoning was simple and dangerous: California regulates the medical profession so heavily that any instruction required for a medical license automatically becomes "government speech" – which means the First Amendment doesn't apply to it at all.

Regulate a profession heavily enough and the government owns every word spoken inside it.

One Trump-appointed Ninth Circuit judge called it "state-sanctioned groupthink" in the en banc dissent.

The Supreme Court majority let that ruling stand, declining to hear the case – Thomas and Alito dissented.

Thomas Named Every Profession California Can Force Into DEI Compliance Next
Thomas wrote nine pages on what the Supreme Court just greenlit – and he warned about California was doing.

"What of other professions whose members California licenses and regulates?" he wrote. "At the next statewide legal conference at which lectures are offered for continuing legal education, could California require a keynote speaker to oppose racial preferences in law firm hiring?"

Thomas wasn't speculating – that was the logical endpoint of the Ninth Circuit's ruling.

Under that logic, any state that licenses a profession – medicine, law, engineering, accounting, counseling – can mandate exactly what licensed professionals say in professional settings.

An engineer teaching a licensed professional development course would need to include the state's preferred messaging on climate policy. A counselor teaching other counselors would affirm gender ideology as settled science, or lose the license that lets her practice.

Thomas went further: "It cannot be the case that compelled speech becomes government speech because the government has compelled the speech."

This isn't the first time California tried this playbook. In 2018, the state told pro-life pregnancy centers they had to post notices advertising nearby abortion clinics – classifying it as professional regulatory speech exempt from First Amendment scrutiny.

The Supreme Court struck it down in NIFLA v. Becerra.

California came back with a different theory – instead of calling it "professional speech," they reclassified it as "government speech." The Ninth Circuit accepted that rebranding, and Thomas described it as using the government-speech doctrine "a cover for censorship" or "a cloak for compelled speech."

Justice Neil Gorsuch also indicated he would have granted certiorari, noting his dissent separately without joining Thomas's written opinion. That's three justices – Thomas, Alito, Gorsuch – and four are needed to take a case. They came up one vote short.

Other states have followed California's lead, passing similar implicit bias mandates for licensed professionals. They're all watching what California just got away with.

The government-speech doctrine was designed for one narrow purpose: letting governments articulate their own positions without being forced into false neutrality.

California turned it into a weapon. Regulate a profession heavily enough, then classify every private instruction delivered under that license as "government speech" – and the First Amendment disappears for every licensed professional in the country.

Thomas warned his colleagues that the Court's own precedent doesn't support this result, and neither does the Constitution.

Chief Justice John Roberts Roberts, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett were each appointed to stop exactly this kind of government overreach. All three passed, joined by Justices Jackson, Sotomayor, and Kagan – though nobody expected the Left side of the Court to fight for free speech.

Thomas left nine pages in the record explaining what comes next.

text:
THE ISLAND | Part 3 of 22

THE WARNINGS: Nine Years Before Anyone Acted

1996.A young artist named Maria Farmer contacts the FBI. She reports that Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell are sexually abusing minors.

Nine years later, Palm Beach police open the first real investigation.

In between, the warnings kept coming. 

So did the praise.

📘 THE CALL

The report. 

Farmer had worked for Epstein. 

The FBI's own record of her complaint, a report dated September 3, 1996, stayed hidden for nearly three decades. The Justice Department released it on December 19, 2025, under the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

What she said. 

According to House Oversight Democrats, she reported that Epstein and his associates were sexually abusing minors and producing child sexual abuse material.

What the FBI did. 

Not enough. 

Farmer's lawyers say the agent didn't follow up. In May 2025, she sued the federal government for negligence.

Who ran the FBI then? 1996 was the Clinton administration. Every administration after it inherited the same file.

🔍 THE PRAISE

October 2002. New York magazine profiles Epstein as an "International Moneyman of Mystery." Two very different men offer glowing quotes.

🔹 Donald Trump: "I've known Jeff for fifteen years. Terrific guy." And: "It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side."
🔹 Bill Clinton, through a spokesperson: "Jeffrey is both a highly successful financier and a committed philanthropist with a keen sense of global markets."

One article. A former Democratic president and a future Republican one. Both later said they knew nothing of his crimes.

🎯 THE STORY THAT GOT CUT

2003. Journalist Vicky Ward writes a Vanity Fair profile of Epstein. She says she had on-the-record accounts from a mother and her daughters. The oldest described Epstein trying to seduce her. Her younger sister was 16.

Ward's account. 

Her editor told her: "Graydon's taking out the women from the piece." She says she was told the editor-in-chief, Graydon Carter, was "sensitive about the young women."

The family. 

The sisters were Maria and Annie Farmer. Annie later testified under her own name at Ghislaine Maxwell's 2021 trial.

Carter's side. He denies the "sensitive" remark. He told Politico: "we didn't have confidence in Ward's reporting," and that she "didn't have the goods."

🕳️ THE PART YOU MISSED

The reviews that skipped it. 

In 2020, the Justice Department's ethics office reviewed how prosecutors handled Epstein in 2007-2008. It didn't examine the 1996 FBI complaint. In December 2025, Rep. Robert Garcia asked the Justice Department's inspector general to investigate both: the FBI's failure in the 1990s, and why later reviews never addressed it.

The math. 

1996 complaint. 2003 story cut. 2005 police investigation. 2008 deal. 2019 arrest. Twenty-three years from the first warning to federal charges.

🛡️ THEIR SIDE

Farmer's account of how the FBI handled her call comes from her lawsuit, not from an official finding. Carter stands by his editorial judgment. Trump says the two had a falling out years before Epstein's arrest, and Clinton says he knew "nothing" about Epstein's crimes. 

Neither has been accused of wrongdoing by prosecutors.

📌 Next, Part 4: Palm Beach. A 14-year-old. A police chief who wanted more. And a state charge that shrank.

text:
$KITE flipped long inside a weak 153-bar range. Kong Cloud scored the event at 11, in the Noise tier.

This is a useful case for understanding why a state change and structural confirmation are separate parts of the model.

The chart frame is a box from 0.0938 to 0.1536. It has four touches on one boundary and three on the other, spans 5.13 ATR, and lacks confirmation from the volume profile. KITE changed state at 0.1374, still inside that box. There was no event at either boundary.

In the Kong Cloud process, a ranging market routes through a structural classification before the score is assembled. The system asks whether price produced a breakout, breakdown, rejection, bounce, or remained inside the established range. Structure carries a weight of 35 in this regime because support and resistance define the frame while price is contained.

The crucial detail is that an established box is frozen. A close beyond a boundary can then be classified against a stable reference, consistent with the classical structural treatment associated with Edwards and Magee. Moving a boundary to accommodate each new close would erase the distinction between a contained move and an actual change in structure.

KITE produced the contained case. Its structural context was inside_range, which assigned a structural factor of zero. The structure component therefore added nothing to the score. This does not invalidate the long state. It says the state change has not received evidence from the part of the model with the largest ranging-regime weight.

The remaining evidence was limited. Volume measured 0.89 times its rolling 20-bar baseline and was declining. That sits in the normal 0.8 to 1.5 band, but the direction of volume offered no added confirmation. Momentum alignment was mixed. The five-day macro reading diverged.

Kong Cloud begins with smoothed state detection to reduce one-bar noise. It then requires three-bar confirmation before recording a flip. That answers one question: has the indicator state changed with enough persistence to count? The scoring layers answer a different question: how much independent evidence agrees with that change?

Separating those questions matters here. A flip can be genuine as an indicator event while remaining analytically weak as a Prime. The Kong Score of 11 records that distinction. It is a measured verdict on the available evidence, without forcing every detected change into a stronger narrative.

The next informative observation is structural. Persistence inside the box would leave the largest ranging component inactive. A close beyond 0.1536 or below 0.0938 would create a boundary event that can be evaluated on its own evidence, including volume behavior. Can the new state survive containment long enough for structure to participate?
